title: Control plane: add fleet readiness states + internal API
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Summary: Introduces a canonical node readiness state model in the control plane and exposes internal (operator-only) APIs to read and mutate readiness for a fleet node. This is the first control-plane building block for provision-to-ready automation (Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready / Quarantined) as defined in ADR-017. The API is intentionally scoped to internal tooling + orchestrators; it is not customer-facing.

Motivation: Today, readiness is inferred indirectly from a mix of kube/node condition signals and ad-hoc fleet scripts. That makes it difficult to enforce gating (e.g. “don’t add nodes to serving pools until validations pass”) and to surface actionable failure reasons. This PR makes readiness explicit, durable, and auditable in the control plane.

What’s in this PR: (1) Data model + migration: Adds fleet_readiness_nodes and fleet_readiness_events tables. Nodes store current_state, last_transition_at, last_heartbeat_at, and a small set of normalized fields for failure_reason_code + failure_reason_message. Events are append-only transition records to support debugging/SLI calculations later. (2) State machine + transitions: Adds a small state transition helper that enforces allowed transitions (Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready; any state -> Quarantined; Quarantined -> Provisioning only via explicit override). Transition validation is done in the control plane; clients cannot write arbitrary states. (3) Internal APIs: Adds REST endpoints under /internal/fleet/readiness: GET /nodes?pool_id=&region=&state= for listing, GET /nodes/{node_id} for detail, POST /nodes/{node_id}/transition for state transitions, and POST /nodes/{node_id}/heartbeat to record agent/orchestrator heartbeats. These endpoints are behind internal authz and require the fleet-operator role. (4) Authz + auditability: Adds authorization checks for all mutate endpoints; read endpoints require fleet-readonly or fleet-operator. Emits structured audit logs for transition actions (actor, node_id, old_state, new_state, reason_code). (5) Basic integration tests: Adds request/response contract tests for the internal API and migration coverage for the new tables.

Not included / follow-ups: This PR does not yet store validation artifacts or per-step durations (coming in a follow-up PR). It also doesn’t enforce readiness gates for joining serving pools (separate PR). Metric emission is minimal here; observability hooks land after API stabilization.

Risk/rollout: Low-risk in production because the new tables and endpoints are additive and unused by default. We will enable write traffic only from the provisioning orchestrator behind a feature flag once downstream is ready. Migration is backwards compatible and safe to run online.

References: ADR-017 (readiness state machine), ENG-4822 (implementation), Slack thread: eng-platform alignment on naming + fields. Tested locally with Postgres + integration test suite; verified authz behavior with internal roles.

Checklist: - [x] DB migration is additive + reversible - [x] Authz checks for all endpoints - [x] Integration tests for transition constraints - [x] Audit log fields reviewed with SRE - [x] OpenAPI updated for internal endpoints
commits: control-plane/db: add fleet readiness tables + indices
control-plane/readiness: implement state enum + transition guard
authz: gate readiness writes behind fleet-operator role
tests: add integration tests for transition validation + authz
review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we make sure only the orchestrator can call transition, not any internal service with a generic token? Also, naming: prefer current_state over readiness_state to avoid confusion with k8s readiness.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated authz to require fleet-operator for transitions; read-only role can list/detail. Renamed column + API field to current_state throughout.

Jordan Lee (review): Transition rules: should Quarantined -> Provisioning be allowed only with an explicit override flag + actor recorded. Also, allow any -> Quarantined is OK, but ensure we prevent Ready -> Validating regressions unless forced.
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented override_required for Quarantined -> Provisioning and blocked Ready -> Validating without override. Transition endpoint now requires {"override": true} for those cases and logs it in audit.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add an audit log entry for all state changes including old/new and actor. Also, avoid storing long failure blobs; keep it short and link to external logs later.
Benji Okafor (author): Added structured audit logger call on every transition. failure_reason_message capped at 512 chars; longer details should live in validation artifacts (follow-up).

Allison Grant (observability): Future-proof: include last_transition_at and last_heartbeat_at as timestamps for SLIs. Also index by pool_id/region/current_state for dashboards.
Benji Okafor (author): Added timestamps and composite index (pool_id, region, current_state).
release_notes: Internal: Control plane now supports explicit fleet readiness state tracking + internal readiness APIs (operator-only).
